the stratigraphy of southeastern New York and northeastern New Jersey is best understood when considered in the context of stratigraphy of the northern Appalachian basin as a whole, and that the report area has been subjected to considerable pre-Oriskanian erosion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Upper Cayugan-Helderbergian stratum in the Green Pond outlier and in the main outcrop area is composed of a series of facies that are arranged in basinward succession.

the Upper Cayugan-early Helderbergian (Rondout Formation, lower 1/2 of the Berkshire Valley Fm., and lower part of the Orrs Mills Mbr.) is represented by a series of shallow marine facies, whereas the late Helder-bergian (Orrs Mills Mbr. and upper 1/2 Berkshire Valley Fm.) is dominated by deep marine facies.
the late Cayuganian and Helderbergan history in the northern Appalachian basin was marked by the development of an east-west trending, northward-deepening, and northward-shoaling sea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stratigraphy of the Green Pond-Schuemunk Mountain outlier is very similar to that of the main outcropping belt.

the stratigraphic units in the outlier can be correlated with those along the main outcrops, and that a series of litho- and paleoenvironmental maps can be constructed to illustrate the evolution of the northern Appalachian basin during late Cayugan-Helderbergian time.
